title: Darwin among the Machines
subtitle: A letter to the editor
pitch: Four years after Darwin's Origin of Species, a young sheep farmer in New Zealand asks whether machines might evolve and one day rule us. The oldest warning on this shelf.

chapters.g: Butler traces machines from the lever to the steamship and treats them as a new kingdom of life, evolving fast.
If machines keep improving like living things, they may one day surpass us. He imagines a time when we serve them.
His satirical answer: destroy every machine now, before it is too late, and go back to a simple life.

ideas: Machines can be seen as evolving.
The servant may become the master.
Humans may come to depend on machines so much they cannot stop.

args.c: Butler wrote partly as satire, and machines of his time had no goals of their own.

questions: Butler wrote as satire. Which parts read as serious today?
What would Butler think of AI agents?

quiz.q: When was 'Darwin among the Machines' published?
